examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Track values at each program point and join incoming paths conservatively. A variable is constant at a join only if every reachable incoming definition has the same constant. Loops require fixed-point iteration. Folding an expression with constant operands differs from propagating a value through variable assignments.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Both branches assign x=7, then code executes y=x*3−1. What constant can y be replaced with?

**Answer: 20.** Both incoming paths agree on x=7, so x remains constant at the join. Fold y=7·3−1=20. If either branch assigned a different value, this replacement would not be justified.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Side effects, aliasing and overflow semantics can invalidate naive substitutions. Only use information guaranteed along every reachable path.

One constant incoming path is insufficient when another path can assign a different value.
